Existentialism quotes

Existentialism names a family of philosophies that treat human existence, freedom, and responsibility as primary—often before abstract systems.

51 passages · 10 voices in this archive selection

Overview

Though diverse, existential writers share concerns with anxiety, authenticity, bad faith, absurdity, and the demand to choose under uncertainty. Kierkegaard and Nietzsche prepare the ground; Sartre, Beauvoir, and Camus make mid-century public debates about freedom and meaning.

Historical notes

Nineteenth-century precursors meet twentieth-century phenomenology and postwar literature. Not all associated figures accepted the label—Camus resisted “existentialist”—yet the cluster remains useful for readers of freedom and meaning.

Core ideas

  • Existence precedes essence for human beings (Sartre’s slogan).
  • Freedom brings responsibility; evasion is bad faith.
  • Meaning may be created, discovered, or confronted as absurd.
  • Concrete situations matter more than empty abstractions.

Thinkers in this archive

Blaise Pascal , Søren Kierkegaard , Jean-Paul Sartre , Albert Camus , Simone de Beauvoir , Simone Weil , José Ortega y Gasset , Karl Jaspers , Paul Tillich , Gabriel Marcel

FAQ

What is existentialism?

It is a philosophical approach emphasizing concrete human existence, freedom, choice, and responsibility.

Is Camus an existentialist?

Camus is often grouped with existential writers but preferred the language of the absurd and revolt; read him alongside, not simply under, Sartre.
